query: How can businesses improve Yelp user satisfaction?

per_column.name: service_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Type of service problem (rude, slow, wrong order, understaffed) is an intervenable operational lever a business can address by changing staffing, training, and processes.

per_column.name: pricing_value_perception
per_column.rationale: Pricing and value perception reflect a configurable business decision (price levels, extra charges, quality-for-price) that an actor can set or change; an intervenable treatment on satisfaction.

per_column.name: staff_conduct_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity of staff conduct is downstream of, and closely tied to, service_issue_type; it is a settable lever via training/supervision. Could also be read as a mediator of service on satisfaction, but is framed as an actionable treatment.

per_column.name: business_category
per_column.rationale: Business category (restaurant, hotel, retail, etc.) is a common cause of both which service/pricing issues arise and baseline satisfaction levels; must be adjusted for to compare interventions across contexts. Not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The columns supply genuinely intervenable treatments (service issue type, pricing/value perception, staff conduct) that a business could actually change, satisfying part (a) of the what-if claim. For part (b), business_category is a legitimate confounder common cause of both treatment exposure and baseline satisfaction and was NOT named in the query, demonstrating the confounder-discovery capability. However, only a single confounder is provided; other obvious common causes (e.g., establishment tier/price segment, location/demographics, prior reputation) are absent, so confounder coverage is thin. The set meets the interventional bar but with limited confounder adjustment.
